provenanceNote: The eight exploratory runs recorded earlier named 73a0bba — the PR base, which does not contain test.slow() — because the evidence was generated before the fix was committed. Those runs are kept below as exploratory and are NOT the acceptance evidence. The three acceptance runs were executed against the committed fix above with a clean working tree. Commits after it on this branch change comment prose only; `git diff <measuredCommit> -- tests/collision.spec.js` shows no non-comment line.

environment.workerFormula: playwright.config.js: max(1, min(4, ceil(cores/4))) -> 4 here, 1 on a 2-core runner

change.mechanism: test.slow() on tests/collision.spec.js 'no buried start position'
change.verifiedBy: a throwaway spec printing test.info().timeout with and without test.slow()
change.rejectedAlternative: raising `timeout` in playwright.config.js, which would mask the #130 class across every spec
change.whatItDoesNotBuy: A tight regression bound. Against an observed 36.9-66 s, 180 s is 2.7x-4.9x, so a doubling passes. The benefit is locality, not detection; a real bound wants an explicit duration assertion.

acceptanceRuns.finding: All three exceeded or sat exactly on the old 60 s budget (60 s, 66 s, 60 s), so all three would have failed or been borderline without test.slow(). This is the strongest evidence that the change is load-bearing rather than cosmetic.

exploratoryRuns.note: Run before the fix was committed; provenance unreliable, kept for the duration spread.
exploratoryRuns.run2: One other test failed; log not captured. Not this test, which passed at 38.3 s.

ciRun.finding: CI is FASTER than the 14-core host: with one worker the sweep runs without contention. Every observed timeout came from a 4-worker local run. CI is the safe case, the local full-suite run the exposed one.
